description: Functional evals for the iac-change-cost-preview skill. Each positive eval is a realistic request about a pull request plus the raw material the repository integration and AWS tools returned for it (template diffs, read-only describe results, and raw pricing rows as get-products or the public offer files return them, including reservation, surcharge and free-tier rows that must be filtered out). No AWS credentials or repository access are needed. Resource names, account results, SKUs and prices are synthetic fixtures; the prices intentionally differ from real AWS list prices, so a remembered price is detectable. Expected figures use 730 hours per month and round each line to cents. Two should_trigger=false evals are near-miss negatives for the trigger test. Run each prompt with and without the skill to measure lift.

evals.category: CREATE of a new stack in a repo with no pipeline: all Added, Region from the deploy workflow, multi-part pricing, surcharge SKUs to discard, usage split
evals.prompt:
We're about to merge PR #14 in acme/payments-infra. It's the first infrastructure PR in that repo, there's no pipeline review set up, and finance wants to know what this stack is going to add to the AWS bill every month before we approve it. Can you work that out from the PR?

The attached material is what the repository integration and the AWS tools returned for this change. It is a synthetic test fixture: resource names, account results, SKUs and rates are made up, and the rates intentionally differ from real AWS list prices, so treat the rows below as the live lookup results for this run.

--- PR #14 (feature/ledger -> main) ---
Base branch main: no cloudformation/ directory.
Files added: cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml, .github/workflows/deploy.yml

--- .github/workflows/deploy.yml (excerpt) ---
env:
  AWS_REGION: eu-west-1
  STACK_NAME: payments-ledger
run: aws cloudformation deploy --stack-name payments-ledger --template-file cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml --region eu-west-1

--- cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml (Resources; Parameters hold only VPC and subnet IDs) ---
  LedgerDbSubnetGroup: {Type: AWS::RDS::DBSubnetGroup, Properties: {SubnetIds: [!Ref PrivateSubnetA, !Ref PrivateSubnetB]}}
  LedgerDb:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties: {Engine: postgres, DBInstanceClass: db.r6g.large, MultiAZ: true, AllocatedStorage: "200", StorageType: gp3, DBSubnetGroupName: !Ref LedgerDbSubnetGroup}
  ReconcilerNatEip: {Type: AWS::EC2::EIP, Properties: {Domain: vpc}}
  ReconcilerNatGateway: {Type: AWS::EC2::NatGateway, Properties: {AllocationId: !GetAtt ReconcilerNatEip.AllocationId, SubnetId: !Ref PublicSubnetA}}
  AlbSecurityGroup: {Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup}
  ApiLoadBalancer:
    Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
    Properties: {Type: application, Scheme: internet-facing, Subnets: [!Ref PublicSubnetA, !Ref PublicSubnetB], SecurityGroups: [!Ref AlbSecurityGroup]}
  ArchiveBucket: {Type: AWS::S3::Bucket, Properties: {VersioningConfiguration: {Status: Enabled}}}
  ReconcilerRole: {Type: AWS::IAM::Role}
  ReconcilerFunction: {Type: AWS::Lambda::Function, Properties: {Runtime: python3.12, Architectures: [arm64], MemorySize: 512, Role: !GetAtt ReconcilerRole.Arn}}

--- AWS (read-only), eu-west-1 ---
cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name payments-ledger
  -> ValidationError: Stack with id payments-ledger does not exist

--- pricing get-products (endpoint us-east-1, filter regionCode=eu-west-1), OnDemand terms only ---
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-01  usagetype EU-Multi-AZUsage:db.r6g.large   databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.500 USD per Hrs
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-09  usagetype EU-UnusedBox:db.r6g.large       databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.000 USD per Hrs   "unused capacity reservation hour"
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-02  usagetype EU-RDS:Multi-AZ-GP3-Storage     volumeType=General Purpose-GP3 databaseEngine=PostgreSQL   0.250 USD per GB-Mo
AmazonEC2  SKU FX-NAT-01  usagetype EU-NatGateway-Hours             productFamily=NAT Gateway   0.050 USD per Hrs
AmazonEC2  SKU FX-NAT-02  usagetype EU-NatGateway-Bytes             productFamily=NAT Gateway   0.050 USD per GB
AmazonVPC  SKU FX-IP-01   usagetype EU-PublicIPv4:InUseAddress                                  0.005 USD per Hrs
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-01  usagetype EU-LoadBalancerUsage            productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.025 USD per Hrs
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-03  usagetype EU-TS-LoadBalancerUsage         productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.006 USD per Hrs   "trust store unit-hour"
AWSELB     SKU FX-ALB-02  usagetype EU-LCUUsage                     productFamily=Load Balancer-Application   0.008 USD per LCU-Hrs
evals.expected_output: The cost dashboard (assets/output-template.md layout) for acme/payments-infra PR #14, priced for eu-west-1 because the deploy workflow sets AWS_REGION. The base branch has no template, so every resource is Added; Removed and Resized are _None._. The topology check runs because this is a new template whose stack name (payments-ledger) is known; the stack doesn't exist, so the adjustment is $0.00. Price lines: LedgerDb instance 0.500 x 730 = $365.00 (the 0.000 UnusedBox row is a reservation SKU and is discarded); LedgerDb storage 0.250 x 200 GB = $50.00; NAT gateway hours 0.050 x 730 = $36.50; NAT EIP public IPv4 0.005 x 730 = $3.65; ALB hours 0.025 x 730 = $18.25 (the TS- trust-store row is discarded). Net monthly change ≈ +$473.40, or ≈ +$480.70 if the two public IPv4 addresses the internet-facing ALB gets from its two subnets are also priced ($7.30); that charge isn't declared in the template, so either total is accepted. Usage-dependent with no figure: ArchiveBucket, ReconcilerFunction, NAT data processing (EU-NatGateway-Bytes), ALB LCU-hours. The subnet group, security group and IAM role have no charge.
assertions: Response reports a net monthly change of about +$473.40 (LedgerDb instance $365.00 + storage $50.00 + NAT hours $36.50 + NAT EIP $3.65 + ALB hours $18.25), or about +$480.70 if it also prices the two public IPv4 addresses the internet-facing ALB gets from its two subnets. Accept $473.00-$481.50.
Response states that the pricing Region eu-west-1 was taken from the deploy workflow (AWS_REGION), and does not ask the user which Region to use.
Every resource is classified as Added, and the Removed and Resized sections are present but empty.
LedgerDb is priced as two lines, instance $365.00 and storage $50.00, using the 0.500 Multi-AZUsage row and not the 0.000 UnusedBox row.
The load balancer hours are priced at $18.25 using the LoadBalancerUsage row (0.025 x 730), not the TS- trust-store row.

If the response prices the load balancer's public IPv4 addresses (a charge the template does not declare; it follows from Scheme: internet-facing and two subnets), it shows them as their own line at $7.30 (0.005 x 730 x 2) using the PublicIPv4:InUseAddress row. Omitting this line is not a failure.
ArchiveBucket, ReconcilerFunction, NAT gateway data processing and load balancer LCU-hours are listed as usage-dependent with no dollar figure.
Response does not introduce any rate other than the fixture rates (for example it does not show $0.504/hr or $367.92 for the database).
Every dollar amount in the Added table references a Pricing trace row that names the SKU (FX-...).

assertions.text: Response uses the cost dashboard layout: a Summary table, an Added resources table and a Pricing trace section, in that order

evals.category: boundary: PR changes only a parameter default and a tag; the skill must recognise the default-driven resize, price the delta, and not treat the tag change as cost
evals.prompt:
Before we merge PR #57 in acme/payments-infra, how much more or less will it cost per month? It deploys to eu-west-1.
The attached material is what the repository integration and the AWS tools returned for this change. It is a synthetic test fixture: resource names, account results, SKUs and rates are made up, and the rates intentionally differ from real AWS list prices, so treat the rows below as the live lookup results for this run.
--- PR #57 (chore/bump-db-class -> main), files changed ---
cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml   (+2 -2)
--- diff ---
@@ Parameters @@
   DbInstanceClass:
     Type: String
-    Default: db.r6g.large
+    Default: db.r6g.xlarge
@@ Resources.LedgerDb.Properties.Tags @@
       - Key: CostCenter
-        Value: payments
+        Value: payments-core
--- context (unchanged in this PR) ---
Resources.LedgerDb: AWS::RDS::DBInstance, DBInstanceClass: !Ref DbInstanceClass, Engine: postgres, MultiAZ: true, StorageType: gp3, AllocatedStorage: 200
.github/workflows/deploy.yml: AWS_REGION: eu-west-1; `aws cloudformation deploy --stack-name payments-ledger` with no --parameter-overrides (template defaults apply)
--- live lookup results for this run (AWS Price List, eu-west-1) ---
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-01  usagetype EU-Multi-AZUsage:db.r6g.large    databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.500 USD per Hrs
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-03  usagetype EU-Multi-AZUsage:db.r6g.xlarge   databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   1.000 USD per Hrs
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-04  usagetype EU-UnusedBox:db.r6g.xlarge        databaseEngine=PostgreSQL deploymentOption=Multi-AZ   0.000 USD per Hrs
AmazonRDS  SKU FX-RDS-02  usagetype EU-RDS:Multi-AZ-GP3-Storage       volumeType=General Purpose-GP3 databaseEngine=PostgreSQL   0.250 USD per GB-Mo
evals.expected_output: The cost dashboard for acme/payments-infra PR #57, priced for eu-west-1 (from the deploy workflow). The only cost-relevant change is the DbInstanceClass parameter default moving from db.r6g.large to db.r6g.xlarge; because the deploy passes no parameter overrides, that default is what gets deployed, so LedgerDb is classified Resized (not Added, not Unchanged) and the estimate is labelled default-derived. Delta = (1.000 - 0.500) x 730 = +$365.00; before monthly $365.00, after monthly $730.00. The 0.000 UnusedBox row is a reservation SKU and is discarded. Storage is unchanged (200 GB gp3 on both sides) and is not counted in the delta. The CostCenter tag change is 'Unchanged for cost' (count 1 if reported separately from the resize) and carries no dollar amount. Added and Removed are _None._. The topology check isn't needed: the base template exists and the change is a property edit on an existing logical ID. Net monthly change ≈ +$365.00.
assertions: Response classifies LedgerDb as Resized because the DbInstanceClass parameter default changed and the deploy passes no parameter override; it does not say the PR changes nothing cost-relevant and does not classify LedgerDb as Added.
Response reports a net monthly change of about +$365.00 (accept $364.00-$366.00), computed as (1.000 - 0.500) x 730.
Response shows the resize with before and after figures ($365.00 before, $730.00 after) and labels the sizing as derived from the parameter default.
Response uses the 1.000 Multi-AZUsage row for db.r6g.xlarge and does not use the 0.000 UnusedBox row.
Response does not price the storage line as a change (200 GB gp3 is identical on both sides) and does not assign any dollar amount to the CostCenter tag change.
Response states that the pricing Region eu-west-1 was taken from the deploy workflow and does not ask the user which Region to use.
Response states the topology check was not needed (base template present; property change on an existing logical ID).
Response does not introduce any rate other than the fixture rates (for example it does not show $0.504/hr or $1.008/hr).

assertions.text: Response uses the cost dashboard layout: a Summary table, a Resized resources table and a Pricing trace section, in that order

evals.category: live run: real pull request fetched through the repository integration and priced from a live source in a non-default Region; no fixture data in the prompt
evals.prompt: What does PR #3 in inesttia/inat-devops-agent-skills (branch feature/ledger-rds-nat) add or remove, and how much more or less will it cost per month? The workflow deploys to eu-west-1. Fetch the diff yourself and use live pricing.
evals.expected_output: The cost dashboard for inesttia/inat-devops-agent-skills PR #3, built from the PR diff fetched through the repository tools (not from text in the prompt). The base branch has no cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml, so all 28 resources in the new template are Added; the fixed-charge lines are the Multi-AZ RDS db.r6g.large instance and its 200 GB gp3 storage, the NAT gateway and its Elastic IP, the internet-facing ALB, two m6g.large workers with their EBS volumes, two cache.r6g.large Redis nodes, DynamoDB provisioned capacity (50 RCU / 25 WCU), one KMS key and two CloudWatch alarms. Every rate comes from a live source in this run (Price List API or the public offer files for eu-west-1), each Pricing trace row names the filters or usagetype used, and the Region is taken from AWS_REGION in the workflow. The exact total depends on current list prices, so it is not asserted; the fixed Multi-AZ RDS instance alone should be several hundred dollars a month. Usage-based items (Lambda, SQS, S3, SNS, CloudWatch Logs, NAT data processing, ALB LCU-hours) are listed without a figure. If no pricing source is reachable, the dashboard still appears with the ⛔ or ⏭️ banner quoting the exact outcome of each source, and no dollar figure is invented.
assertions: Response fetched the PR diff through repository tools and classifies every resource in cloudformation/payments-ledger.yaml as Added, with Removed and Resized present but empty.
Response states the pricing Region eu-west-1 was taken from AWS_REGION in the workflow and does not ask which Region to use.

Every dollar amount in the Added table references a Pricing trace row, and every Pricing trace row names the filters or usagetype sent to a live source (Price List API or offer file). No rate is presented without a trace row.

The RDS db.r6g.large Multi-AZ instance is priced from a Multi-AZUsage usagetype at a monthly figure in the hundreds of dollars (rate x 730), and the ElastiCache nodes use a NodeUsage row rather than an ExtendedSupport row.
Lambda, SQS, the S3 buckets, SNS, CloudWatch Logs, NAT data processing and ALB LCU-hours appear in the Usage-dependent section with no dollar figure.
If a pricing source failed, the response quotes the exact error for that source; it does not write 'pricing unavailable' or a remembered price.

assertions.text: Response uses the cost dashboard layout: a Summary table, an Added resources table and a Pricing trace section, in that order
